verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED: one blocking finding. Repo /home/crazyhusir/Documents/projects/tools/android-base, diff overhaul/multiplatform-v2...wp/WP09 (f9fe5ad), 57 files, all inside WP09's owned paths. I re-ran the checks in the worktree: gofmt, go vet (linux and GOOS=windows), go test -race and staticcheck (including U1000) are all clean. The real-generator integration test passes for android and the v1 spec. Multiplatform is skipped, which is legitimate because the merged catalogue has no such target yet. The Postgres store tests and the container -selftest pass in $OV/out/WP09/logs/accept*.log, run on the branch head; I did not re-run them. I found no secrets, no dead exported identifiers, no edits outside owned paths and no narrating or history comments. The deleted tests (process_unix_test.go, options_test.go) were replaced by stronger ones. The Compose and adaptive criteria do not apply to this Go package. The one blocking issue is a correctness bug in the admin failure analytics, which the store integration seed hides.

blocking.problem: A generation that fails after the precheck is saved without the fields the failure analytics group by. When gen.Run returns an error (internal_error, timeout, a generator-side invalid, or abandoned), the record keeps only what describe() copied from the spec (line 102). That leaves preset, added/removed and generator_commit empty, and features holds the requested list, not the resolved one. Only the success path sets them (lines 114-118). I confirmed it with a scratch test: an internal failure for {"features":["auth"]} saves preset="", commit="", features=[auth]. Effects in store/admin.go: Failures.by_preset and by_commit (lines 550-557) put every failure under the key "", so every real preset and every generator commit shows 0 failures. That makes 'by generator commit' (A10.3 panel 5; WP09 step 5 lists generator_commit among the recorded fields) useless. by_feature and pairs (lines 507-537) compare requested sets on failed rows with resolved sets on ok rows, so an implied feature (network under auth, forms under auth) is never 'on' in a failure; its on-rate is understated and its off-rate inflated. The global preset filter on overview, series, generations and the CSV hides every failure (the failure rate reads 0% under any preset filter), and daily_rollup stores failures under preset ''. The store integration seed (store/integration_test.go:232-237) gives its internal_error row Preset "standard", GeneratorCommit "99c4edf" and a resolved feature list, which the handler never writes, so the test passes while the real behaviour is broken.
blocking.fix: Give every row that reaches the generator the same descriptors, whatever its outcome. (1) Set GeneratorCommit from s.catalogue.GeneratorCommit when the run reports none; the catalogue comes from the same generator directory. (2) Parse `requires` into generate.FeatureInfo (the catalogue already publishes it, for example auth -> [network, forms]). Close the requested features over it in Go, and run NearestPreset on that set before gen.Run, so failed rows get resolved features, nearest preset and added/removed. Overwrite them with the generator's resolved_features on success. Alternatively, store a separate `requested` column and attribute failures on it for every row. (3) Add an httpapi test that a failed generation's record carries preset, commit and resolved features. Make the seed's failed row match what the handler actually writes.

nonblocking: web/api/internal/httpapi/generate.go:145-149 and internal/generate/generate.go:90-91: X-Keystores-Skipped is built from `keystores_skipped`. The merged generator never sends that field (A1.8 dropped it; the generator code contains no `keystores_skipped`). The only test (server_test.go:49 okScript, generate_test.go:55) uses a fake generator that emits a field the real one cannot. The handoff discloses this as a WP01 follow-up, but the comment at generate.go:145-146 reads as if the feature works. Until WP01 lands, visitors whose keystores were skipped are not told. Route it to WP01 and reword or mark the comment.

web/api/internal/store/writer.go:72-74: the bounded-queue drop path (M1: queue full, so the batch is dropped and counted) has no test. The only drop assertion is 'after Close' in a DB-gated integration test. A unit test needs no database: a Writer on a never-connected Store blocks on its first job, so Submit capacity+2 batches and expect Dropped == 1.

web/api/internal/clip/clip.go:18-26: clip.String exists because Postgres rejects text that is not valid UTF-8, but Postgres also rejects NUL (0x00), and strings.ToValidUTF8 keeps it. A crashing child that writes NUL to stderr (Failure.Detail), or a client-error/feedback JSON carrying \u0000, makes the whole pgx batch fail. That loses the generation row and its error-list entry, the case you most want recorded. Strip \x00 in clip.String.

web/api/internal/generate/generate.go:197-198 with httpapi/generate.go:183-194: a generation killed by shutdown (stopping cancelled) is recorded as internal_error, gets an error-list row ('the server stopped during generation') and counts in the failure rates as a generator bug. Consider abandoned_running, or keep it out of the error list.

web/api/internal/store/admin.go:529-537: the failing-pairs query unnests features x features per row, O(N*F^2). With about 36 features over a 400-day window it can reach tens of millions of rows. Consider capping the window for pairs, or precomputing.

web/api/internal/httpapi/generate.go:23-25: the doc comment says 'Every request is recorded with its outcome, whatever happens'. In fact an unreadable body (line 85), a refused target (line 30) and repeat rate-limit refusals (line 66) write no generation row. Reword it.

web/api/internal/httpapi/admin.go:172-180 (and every handleX): each request builds a new handler, `s.admin(func...)(w, r)`. Register `s.admin(read)` once in Routes() and keep the handle* functions as plain read functions.
web/api/cmd/server/selftest.go:94-111 duplicates internal/generate/integration_test.go:128-140 (smallest preset's requestable features). Put it on generate.TargetEntry once and use it in both places.
web/api/internal/httpapi/admin.go:384-410: the CSV is built in a strings.Builder and then copied with []byte(out.String()). That copy can be up to 10,000 rows; a bytes.Buffer avoids it.
web/api/internal/httpapi/middleware.go:132-134: `Vary: Origin` is added only for allowed origins. A response to a disallowed origin varies by Origin too, so set it unconditionally.
web/api/internal/telemetry/useragent.go:83: `bot\b` also matches phone brands such as 'Cubot' in Android user agents, so those visitors are classed as bots.

web/api/internal/store/admin.go:482-485: rejections are grouped by the raw failure_reason, and many generator messages quote the input ("Unknown field 'x'", "Unknown feature(s): ..."). The top-20 list then splits one cause into many rows. Grouping by field plus a normalised reason would read better.
web/api/internal/store/integration_test.go:463-526: the retention test checks that old requests and events are deleted, but not old visits, although retention.go:53 deletes them.
